question: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
answer: Start with the claim and legal actor, establish permission and the authoritative record, then trace instruction, resources, settlement, books and remedy. The nine-step research method preserves six legal layers instead of treating a token movement as the whole transaction.

sections.title: Search the complete records
sections.sub: Search names, page or question numbers and the full saved wording. Every card retains its source and exact complete-reference link.

groups.label: The nine steps from a claimed right to a repairable result

items.title: Name the claim
kv: What right is being created, transferred, pledged, redeemed, or paid?
Start with the instrument and obligation. A share, entitlement, bank deposit, token, collateral interest, and payment instruction carry different rights and obligors.
Instrument terms; named obligor; holder-rights description; governing-law clause.
A statement of who owes what to whom under which terms.
Technical possession or a token transfer is not a complete description of legal ownership or discharge.

items.title: Draw the actor perimeter
kv: Which legal entity performs each function?
Separate parent, regulated subsidiary, depository, clearing agency, bank, transfer agent, wallet provider, network, and vendor. One organization can wear several hats; each has separate duties.
Legal operator; regulated subsidiary; service provider; supervisor.
Entity chart; registration or charter; service agreement; supervisory route.
A role map for issuer, recordkeeper, operator, cash obligor, risk manager, and remedy authority.
A shared brand, partnership, or technology stack does not merge legal entities or permissions.

items.title: Establish permission
kv: What allows this entity to perform this function now?
Match the activity to a live authority: terms, registration, operating circular, rulebook, designation, order, exemption, or no-action position. Keep scope and effective date attached.
Statute or regulation; registration/order/letter; effective rulebook; scope and expiry terms.
A permission statement with its date, product, participant, and volume limits.
A proposal, pilot, announcement, or generic FMI label grants no unlisted permission.

items.title: Identify the authoritative record
kv: If books disagree, which record decides the holder, balance, or obligation?

Issuer registers, transfer-agent files, depository entitlement books, bank accounts, and networks can each describe a different legal relationship. Identify the controlling record for this issue and event.
Issuer; recordkeeping transfer agent; depository; bank; network operator.
Recordkeeping agreement; record clause; reconciliation design; correction rights.
A record hierarchy and named reconciliation point.
A distributed ledger can be linked to a master file without becoming the legal register for every asset on it.

items.title: Bind the instruction
kv: Who may send, validate, and delegate an instruction?
A valid instruction has an authorized sender, authentication, eligibility checks, and rules for rejection, cancellation, queueing, and delegation.
Customer or participant; bank or broker; operator; technology provider.
Access agreement; authentication rules; instruction lifecycle; vendor-control terms.
A trace from mandate to accepted instruction, including who can stop it before execution.
A transmitted message, signed wallet action, or broadcast transaction is not necessarily accepted or irrevocable.

items.title: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
kv: Who matches, nets, collateralizes, funds, or guarantees it?
Some routes pass instructions onward; others create CCP obligations, prefunded positions, or bank-credit exposure. Map margin, collateral, liquidity, netting, and default resources.
CCP; clearing member; settlement bank; liquidity provider; collateral manager.
Clearing rules; margin/liquidity rules; funding-account terms; default waterfall.
A resources map of gross and net obligation, pledged resources, funding source, and residual exposure.
Fast execution or a smaller net payment does not prove liquidity, collateral, or default exposure disappeared.

items.title: Settle each leg and name finality
kv: What asset moves, in which accounts, and when is each obligation final?

Securities delivery, cash posting, token transfer, payout, and redemption can have different finality points. Name whether the event is technical confirmation, book-entry posting, contractual discharge, or statutory finality.
Settlement operator; depository; bank; cash issuer; participant.
Settlement rule; cash-asset identity; account-entry timing; finality and insolvency clause.
A two-leg settlement receipt with named assets, timestamps, and finality rules.
A confirmed ledger event does not prove the other leg, legal discharge, redemption, or bank availability.

items.title: Post, reconcile and service
kv: Which books update, and who administers rights after settlement?

Completion creates customer, participant, depository, transfer-agent, issuer, and sometimes network postings. Servicing covers distributions, votes, corporate actions, maturity, redemption, and reporting.
Posting records; reconciliation schedule; servicing agreement; exception reports.
A reconciled record chain and named administrator for ongoing holder rights.
A transaction receipt does not prove all books reconciled or later servicing occurred.

items.title: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
kv: Who can correct an error, what happens on default or outage, and what proves performance?
A durable process names correction powers, reversals, disputes, collateral realization, loss allocation, recovery, and wind-down. Separate written controls from observed stress.
Operator; supervisor; default manager; service provider; affected holder.
Correction rule; default/recovery plan; loss-allocation rule; incident or stress record.
A remedy map naming actor, loss bearer, and evidence level.
Immutability or a service promise does not remove insolvency, correction, or loss-allocation questions.

items.title: FMI standards and domestic implementation
kv: PFMI provides the international framework. U.S. implementation separates Title VIII designation, Board risk standards under Regulation HH, SEC clearing-agency rules and the Fed’s policy for its own systems.
Which rule actually applies to this legal operator and function?
HH risk-standard scope excludes SEC-registered clearing agencies and CFTC-registered DCOs. Transfer-agency functions alone do not automatically establish FMU status.
